THE CORDIAL TIER STRUCTURE IS THE REAL DECISION, and all 12 disagreements are downstream of it. SPIRIT_TIER contains zero liqueurs, cordials, aperitifs or vermouths — it only ever tiered base spirits, so all 21 Liqueur rows plus the 3 Apertif rows are unprecedented. The only anchor in existence is Metaxa Ouzo = Call, published in the Aug 2026 sheet. The 20 costed cordials run $0.61-$2.03/oz with no gap over 8% anywhere in the lower half, so ANY call/premium line drawn there is arbitrary — including mine. Decide once: (a) ratify call-as-default with premium reserved for the craft set (what this list does), or (b) flatten all cordials to a single tier, which the cost distribution actually supports better. Option (b) makes 10 of the 12 disagreements evaporate.

THE TIER LADDER RUNS BACKWARDS FROM INTUITION AND THAT NEEDS OWNER SIGN-OFF BEFORE ANY OF THIS PRICES. Because price = cost / target_pour_cost and the target RISES with tier (well 15% to superPremium 22%), the well tier yields the HIGHEST price per dollar of cost — a 47% spread on identical cost. Promoting a bottle to a higher tier CUTS its price. VERIFIED live: Buchanan's 12 (superPremium, $1.2421/oz) prices $9 while Tanqueray (well, $1.0564/oz — a CHEAPER bottle) prices $11. Confirm this is intended before it reaches GoTab.

RE-DERIVING PRICES AT TODAY'S COSTS WOULD MARK DOWN THE PRESTIGE AGAVE BLOCK, HARD. Live bar_sku costs are materially below the May 2026 study for Casamigos and Herradura Silver. At today's cost and mapped tier the formula outputs: Casamigos Blanco $9 (sells ~$14), Casamigos Reposado $9, Casamigos Anejo $9 (sells ~$14), Herradura Silver $7 (sells ~$12). The tiers are not the problem — the cost fell and the price did not. Decide deliberately whether to take the markdown, hold price and bank the margin, or re-tier. This is the largest dollar exposure in the whole exercise.

Worthy Park Single Estate Reserve: premium (both passes, matching the published Aug 2026 sheet at $19) vs superPremium ($17). Note the direction — superPremium LOWERS it. At $2.4826/oz it is the most expensive rum by 39% and above 5 of the 7 superPremium whiskies. Tell: the Aug sheet already withholds its Mixed button, which is the superPremium treatment, so it is half-tiered that way already. Owner ruling.

Siete Leguas Anejo: premium ($14) vs superPremium ($13). Both passes said premium per the Aug 2026 sheet, so it is not a disagreement — but every OTHER anejo you carry (Don Julio, Patron, Herradura, Casamigos) is superPremium in the map. Decide whether 'anejo' is a tier rule or whether cost is. If someone later 'fixes' this to match the pattern, the price drops. It is not a typo.

Bacardi Limon: flavored ($6) vs well ($7). Both passes chose flavored, but the map is genuinely inconsistent here — Malibu Coconut (a flavored rum) is tiered WELL while Absolut Vanilia/Raspberri are FLAVORED. In practice 'flavored' in this map means sweet flavored whisk(e)y plus Absolut, not any flavored spirit. Worth ruling explicitly since it also governs future line extensions.

SHRINKAGE COVERAGE GAPS — four categories you actively carry have NO key in SHRINKAGE_BY_CAT and silently take the 1.02 default: Brandy (all 4 piscos), Champagne (2), Vermouth (4), Mixers (1). Notably Cognac gets 1.052 while Brandy — also a brandy — gets 1.02. Separately, 3 rows have a NULL bar_sku.category (HENDRICK'S GIN, BITTER TRUTH GOLDEN FALERNUM, RISATA MOSCATO), so Hendrick's misses Gin's 1.024 and Bitter Truth misses Liqueur's 1.028. Under 1% price impact each, but the categories should be set and the four missing shrink keys decided.

13 SKUs DO NOT FIT THE SIX MENU CATEGORIES and are flagged Other-: 5 Other-Cognac, 4 Other-Pisco, 3 Other-Aperitif, 4 Other-Vermouth, 3 Other-Sparkling, 1 Other-Mixer (18 rows total across those tags). Cognac needs a real home — five bottles including two $150-190 luxury pours; a 7th category or fold into Whiskey, but not under Liqueurs/Cordials. Pisco has no natural home in six and you carry FOUR of them, already tier-split two rungs. Aperol/Campari/Lillet fold naturally into Liqueurs/Cordials.

8 of the 116 rows are NOT SPIRITS and qualify only because count_unit='bottle': 4 vermouths, Korbel, Maschio Prosecco, Risata Moscato, and an agave syrup. Their tiers in the final list are nominal placeholders and a pour-cost tier is the wrong instrument for wine-by-the-glass and for a syrup. Confirm they are out of scope for the pour-button rework.

Should there be a 5th tier ABOVE superPremium? Four SKUs sit above $5/oz (Remy XO $5.93, Clase Azul $5.83, Martell $5.61, Don Julio 1942 $5.45) with nothing at all between $2.48 and $5.45. They currently share the 22% target with Don Julio Anejo at $2.18 — a 2.7x cost spread on one target pour cost.

Scotch as its own menu category. All 7 are assigned to Whiskey here so the data drops into your stated six, but the current GoTab menu ALREADY splits 'Scotch Options' from 'Whiskey Options', and 5 of the 7 are superPremium — burying them in a list that opens with Fireball and Jack Daniel's is a positioning downgrade. If you keep six, at least put the scotches as a contiguous block at the bottom of Whiskey.

Carpano duplicate rows: Antica Formula exists at 1L AND 375ml, Dry at 1L AND 375ml — same liquid, two rows each. Mechanical cost banding would put one liquid in two tiers ($0.99/oz vs $1.35/oz for Antica), so both are pinned to their 1L reference here. Also note Antica 1L is the ONLY row in all 116 where wac_cost and last_cost differ ($33.50 vs $37.62) — the methodology's coalesce(wac, last) takes $33.50 while the Aug doc records $37.62 as the newest buy. Same duplicate-size trap is arriving for Appleton, Diplomatico and Harvey's. Decide the rule: tier the PRODUCT, band on a reference size.

Appleton Estate Signature: call ($7) vs well ($8). Both passes chose call, but it is not in SPIRIT_TIER and the POS currently prices it with the wells while its cost/oz ($0.8288) is above every mapped well. Low stakes — it is discontinued and draining — but note that once it drains rum has NO call tier at all, jumping from wells under $0.74 straight to premium at $1.31.
